subject: COVID-19 Metrics and Special Education Contingency Planning
overview: The Committee voted to hold a meeting to revise district COVID-19 metrics in alignment with new state guidance and requested a formal contingency plan for special education services during potential emergency closures. Discussions also addressed facility upgrades, student virus testing, and the challenges of reverse-remote instruction due to staff accommodations.

items.title: Routine Business and Subcommittee Reports
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes from November 2nd, bills, and payrolls, and tabled the Communications Subcommittee report.

items.title: School Calendar Policy Change
items.summary: Approved a policy change to finalize the school calendar in November of the preceding academic year to facilitate family planning.

items.title: Building and Grounds Report
items.summary: Reviewed facility upgrades at the vocational high school, accessibility concerns regarding the front entrance ramp, and funding gaps for capital projects including bathrooms and generators.

items.title: Public Participation on Laptops and Transportation
items.summary: Addressed inquiries regarding the funding sources for teacher laptops and safety protocols for students utilizing public transportation.

items.title: Superintendent's Update and Reopening Phases
items.summary: Provided updates on the phased return of vocational students, food distribution statistics, and the need for additional classroom monitors to support the hybrid model.

items.title: COVID-19 Public Health and Testing Update
items.summary: Received a report on local infection rates and the planned transition to weekly student surveillance testing starting in December.

items.title: Discussion on District COVID-19 Metrics
items.summary: Approved holding a meeting to update district health metrics to align with revised state guidance following concerns that existing policy required a transition to remote learning that was not being followed.

items.title: Instructional Innovations for Vulnerable Students
items.summary: Presented digital tools and community-based learning strategies used for special education and English Learner students during the pandemic.

items.title: Remote Academy and Reverse-Remote Instruction
items.summary: Reviewed elementary and secondary remote learning models and discussed the implementation of 'reverse remote' instruction for in-person students whose teachers have medical accommodations.

items.title: Special Education Contingency Plan
items.summary: Approved a motion to develop a formal contingency plan ensuring the seamless delivery of services to the most vulnerable students in the event of an emergency district-wide closure.

items.title: SNAP GAP and Food Security Report
items.summary: Received a presentation on the high rate of food insecurity in Medford and barriers preventing eligible families from accessing federal nutrition benefits.
